newsitem.title: USA: Cabot sells TUCO unit for about $77 mln.
newsitem.headline: Cabot sells TUCO unit for about $77 mln.

text.p: Cabot Corp said on Friday it had sold its TUCO unit, which owns coal inventory in Texas and administers contracts with coal mines and railroads, for $77 million plus net balance sheet adjustments.
Cabot said it sold TUCO as of September 30 to two Colorado companies -- Republic Financial Corp and an affiliate of NexGen Resources Corp.
The sale included all of TUCO's coal inventory and coal contract operations, it said.

TUCO has coal inventory at two coal-fueled power plants owned by Texas-based Southwestern Public Service Co. It also administered contracts with coal mines, railroads and the coal-handling operator for Southwestern, Cabot said.
TUCO supplies Southwestern plants with about eight million tons of coal a year. Cabot said this long-term contract would continue after the sale.
Southwestern had unsuccessfully sought permission from the Texas Public Utility Commission to purchase TUCO, Cabot said.

NexGen is a natural resource management and development firm. Republic is a privately held financial services company specializing in structured financing and portfolio and asset acquisitions, Cabot said.
